newsitem.title: KUWAIT: Kuwait's bourse bows under Central Bank curbs.
newsitem.headline: Kuwait's bourse bows under Central Bank curbs.

text.p: Kuwait Stock Exchange's index dropped 3.5 percent in three days after the Central Bank placed curbs on lending for equity trading.
The index, which rose 4.6 precent last week to a record 2,439.9 points last Wednesday, fell 27 points on Monday to 2,354.2 following a 49.2 point drop the previous day.

The Central Bank has ordered local banks to stop extending margin loans and to diversify guarantees required against lending for securities trading after the daily value edged back on Wednesday towards the record 125.8 million dinars reached in a single session on April 28.
Trade value on Monday was around 50 million dinars compared with a daily average of 76.6 million dinars last week and 39 million dinars the week before that.
"The rise in activity on the bourse attentioned them (Central Bank) to the fact that they need to further develop tools to control the rise in risk-taking activities by banks," a senior banker said.
Economists said the bank was not trying to interfere with the bourse. "It is trying to protect banks against any eventuality," said a banker.
Economists have expected a correction that some thought could be "painful" if the activity in the market continued to rise.
Loans for securities trading stand at 425 million dinars of which 96 million dinars were margin loans, the Central Bank said. The figure need to be reduced by 130 million dinars by the end of 1997.
Leading Kuwaiti economist Jassem al-Saadoun said: "The amount is not too large...With a trade average of about 50 million dinars a day the market can get over the impact of the curbs in a few weeks."
